newsitem.title: UK: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - April 3.
newsitem.headline: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - April 3.

text.p: ....REUTERS WORLDWIDE ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST.....
Reuters news from around the world on Advertising, Marketing, the Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING AND MARKETING:

LONDON - Cordiant Plc has set up a joint venture advertising agency in Moscow by teaming up with Russia's Video International Group of Companies, the British company says. The new agency, to be known as Bates VIAG Saatchi & Saatchi Advertising, will have combined billings of over $60 million.

CHICAGO - McDonald's Corp. is rolling out its 55-cent promotion at breakfast, a move analysts say will help the fast-food giant test the waters before it discounts its hamburgers. America's biggest fast-food chain will offer its four breakfast sandwiches for 55 cents starting Friday.

PARIS - Havas Advertising, a unit of Havas, had the highest 1996 revenues among French advertising agencies, according to an annual league table from the Association des Agences-Conseils en Communication. Havas in 1996 had gross revenues of 1.83 billion francs ($325.2 million), followed by Publicis Com at 1.27 billion francs and DDB Needham at 743.0 million francs.
AMSTERDAM - Dutch electronics group Philips Electronics says it will not renew its contract to sponsor the European Champions League.

MUNICH - Munich advertising agency ServicePlan says it wants to make the Internet safe for advertisers with a new central database which monitors the success of advertisements in reaching their target audiences. With the Plan.Net media system, advertisers can see how many people have clicked on their logo, as well as open a databse of available Internet ad space.

MOLINE, Illinois - Deere & Co, which manufactures turf maintence and other capital equipment, said on Wednesday it was in a sponsorship agreement with the Professional Golf Association Tour to provide golf course equipment and sponsor a PGA golf tournament.
MEDIA AND THE INTERNET:

NEW YORK - CompuServe Corp is in talks to be acquired by America Online Inc, a move that would bring new members to AOL, beef up its network and expand its corporate and international presence, industry sources say. Earlier, CompuServe and H&R Block Inc, which owns 80 percent of the computer online service, confirmed market rumors that they were in discussions for a possible "business combination" involving CompuServe.

WASHINGTON - Two Washington-area firms bid a total of $173 million at a government auction for the rights to provide a new breed of radio service that can be heard coast-to-coast and offers CD-quality reception. American Mobile Radio Corp., a unit of American Mobile Satellite Corp. of Reston, Va., placed a winning bid of $89.9 million at a Federal Communications Commission sale for one of two licenses to offer digital audio radio. Washington-based CD Radio Inc. put down a top bid of $83.3 million for the other license.

SAN FRANCISCO, Calif. - Web TV Networks Inc says it will work with Sun Microsystems Inc to develop a "Java for TV" initiative bringing new features of the Internet to television. In a keynote address at Sun's JavaOne industry conference here, Sun executives demonstrated how a WebTV could use Java on a television set to browse through TV programs and select TV channels or Internet pages.

CANBERRA - Brierley Investments Ltd has again called for the Australian government to relax foreign ownership restrictions as part of its cross-media ownership review, a newspaper report says. Brierly executive director Rod Price told The Sydney Morning Herald newspaper it made no sense for the government not to review foreign ownership rules in the context of the cross-media ownership review.

HOUSTON - Dow Jones & Co Inc has asked a U.S. federal judge to overturn a record $222.7 million judgment levied against it in a libel suit, warning that the award would have a "staggering effect" on journalism if allowed to stand. The company, which owns the Wall Street Journal, said in court documents that "the enormity of the jury's verdict in this case cannot be overstated."
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS AND MARKETS:

CAPE TOWN - South African wine exports increased to 11.1 million cases in 1996, earning 550 million rand ($124.4 million) in foreign exchange, co-operative KWV says in its latest annual report. The co-operative said wine exports had "snowballed" in the past few years surging by 1,300 percent from the 855,000 cases in 1990.

LONDON - The UK's leading food supermarket chain, Tesco, is predicting 400 per cent growth in sales of organic foods by the year 2000, bringing their value to 50 million stg ($82 million), a company spokesman says

PARIS - French food firms' sales rose by two percent in 1996 despite a consumer scare sparked by mad cow disease, national agro-food industries association ANIA reports. Sales rose to 756.9 billion francs last year from 742.1 billion in 1995 as consumers, concerned about food quality and safety, turned to top of the line brands, president Victor Scherrer said.

SYDNEY - Australian beverage group Coca-Cola Amatil Ltd has transformed itself into the largest Coca-Cola bottler outside the United States by unveiling a A$3.4 billion deal with San Miguel Corp of the Philippines. Under the surprise agreement, C-C Amatil would issue 293 million shares to acquire San Miguel soft drink subsidiary Coca Cola Bottler Philippines Inc, which is owned 70 percent by San Miguel and 30 percent by The Cola Cola Co.

LONDON - A move by Britain's top clothing retailer Marks & Spencer Plc into mail order looks set to raise the profile of home shopping in Britain and put more pressure on established players in the declining agency market, analysts say.
CONSUMER TRENDS:

COLOMBO - Sri Lanka could levy additional tax on alcohol and tobacco to raise funds to improve its health services, government officials say. They say a task force on the health sector has recommended that each cigarette be taxed an additional two cents and every bottle of alcohol 50 cents.

SINGAPORE - Westin Hotels & Resorts plans to double the number of hotels and resorts in the Asia-Pacific region over the next few years, regional president Theodore Teng says. The areas targeted for growth were China, Hong Kong, India, Australia and New Zealand.

OAXACA, Mexico - A potent and earthy Mexican liquor is hitting the export trail, but beware: even locals take it with more than a pinch of salt. Mezcal, tequila's wayward half-brother, had for centuries been the socially frowned-on drink of Mexican peasants. Curiously, that same drink is now developing a cachet all its own in connoisseur drinking dens as far afield as New York, London and Taiwan.
